blocks.text: Fever can result from infectious and non-infectious conditions.
**Examination pearl:** Fever is a regulated rise in body temperature due to an increased hypothalamic set point, unlike hyperthermia.

**Clinical pearl:** Prolonged fever requires a structured history, physical examination, targeted investigations and repeated reassessment rather than indiscriminate antibiotic use.

subsections.subsection_title: 8.3 Causes of fever of unknown origin (FUO)

items.text: Temperature of at least 38.3°C on several occasions.

blocks.text: Modern definitions also include healthcare-associated, neutropenic and HIV-associated FUO.

blocks.text: Other causes include fungal sepsis, particularly Candida in high-risk patients.
**Important:** Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. It is not simply the presence of bacteria in the bloodstream.

blocks.text: **Definition:** Septic shock is a subset of sepsis involving circulatory and cellular/metabolic abnormalities. Clinically, it is characterised by vasopressor requirement to maintain MAP of at least 65 mmHg and lactate above 2 mmol/L despite adequate volume resuscitation.

content_groups.group_title: Why is falciparum malaria particularly dangerous?

items.text: Sequestration of infected erythrocytes in small blood vessels.

blocks.text: **WHO severe malaria manifestations – mnemonic: COMA SHOCK**
Additional recognised manifestations include hypoglycaemia, jaundice with other severe features and hyperparasitaemia.
**Important:** Severe malaria is a medical emergency. It requires urgent parenteral artesunate and supportive management according to current treatment protocols.
Blackwater fever refers to massive intravascular haemolysis causing haemoglobinuria, classically associated with severe falciparum malaria.
HIV causes progressive depletion and dysfunction of CD4 T lymphocytes, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections.

blocks.text: **Examination pearl:** An opportunistic infection may be the first presentation of previously undiagnosed HIV infection.
